claim: A deepfake detector that fuses semantic and artifact evidence with an evidential rule can say when it is likely to be wrong: its uncertainty is high mainly on the images it misclassifies, and it is better calibrated than the same detector trained to make deterministic predictions. Supported only if, on unseen datasets, misclassified images concentrate at high uncertainty while correct ones sit near zero; if discarding the most uncertain predictions raises accuracy steadily as more are discarded, more than for the deterministic baseline; and if expected calibration error is at most half that of the deterministic version on each test set.

experiments: Fix the training and evaluation protocol. Setup: train only on FaceForensics++ at c23 compression with the DeepfakeBench preprocessing; CLIP ViT-L/14 kept frozen with LoRA (rank 8) on its attention layers; augmentation with Gaussian blur, JPEG compression and colour jitter; AdamW, learning rate 1e-4, batch 128, 20 epochs, one A100. Report video-level AUC on two protocols: cross-dataset on six unseen sets (Celeb-DF v2, DFD, DFDC, DeeperForensics, WildDeepfake, Celeb-DF v3), and cross-manipulation on eight face-swap methods from DF40, which share the FaceForensics++ source footage so that only the forgery method changes.

Check that uncertainty flags errors. Setup: on FaceForensics++ and the unseen Celeb-DF v2, DFDC and DFD, plot the fused uncertainty separately for correct and incorrect predictions, and plot accuracy against the fraction of most-uncertain samples rejected, compared with the deterministic baseline. Result: correct predictions cluster near zero uncertainty and misclassifications mostly at high uncertainty; accuracy rises monotonically as more uncertain samples are rejected and stays above the baseline curve, with a large gain on DFD from rejecting only the top 10%.

Measure calibration against a deterministic version of the same model. Setup: expected calibration error on Celeb-DF v2, DFD and MobileFaceSwap for the cross-entropy, mean-fusion variant and for the full model. Result: 0.13 / 0.15 / 0.19 (average 0.16) for the deterministic variant against 0.07 / 0.07 / 0.08 (average 0.07).
